data.title: Steady Start Seen For Japan Stock Market
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - The Japan stock market on Wednesday wrote a finish to the two-day slide in which it had stumbled almost 2,300 points or 3.8 percent. The Nikkei 225 now sits just above the 59,020-point plateau and it may tick higher again on Thursday.

The global forecast for the Asian markets is murky, with Middle East tensions likely offset by sinking crude oil prices and bargain hunting among the technology stocks. The European markets were down and the U.S. bourses were mixed and the Asian markets figure to split the difference.

The Nikkei finished modestly higher on Wednesday as gains from the technology and retail sectors were capped by weakness among the financial shares.

For the day, the index gained 163.85 points or 0.28 percent to finish at 59,024.28 after trading between 58,279.26 and 59,630.95.

The lead from Wall Street is weak as the major averages opened mixed but turned lower before recovering in the afternoon to finish mixed.

The Dow tumbled 561.25 points or 1.11 percent to finish at 50,198.17, while the NASDAQ climbed 101.50 points or 0.42 percent to close at 24,429.88 and the S&P 500 fell 16.90 points or 0.23 percent to end at 7,323.63.

The choppy trading on Wall Street came as traders digested earnings news from AI giant and market leader Nvidia (NVDA), which reported better than expected fiscal third quarter results and raised its revenue guidance.

Investors may also have been looking forward to Claude developer Anthropic's initial public offering later this week.

Gold stocks showed a substantial move to the downside, while pharmaceutical, healthcare and banking stocks also saw considerable weakness.

Crude oil prices tumbled on Wednesday following a report that U.S. crude oil inventories increased much more than expected in the last week. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery was down $2.92 or 3.4 percent to $83.09 a barrel.

Closer to home, Japan will provide September numbers for core machinery orders later this morning, with forecasts suggesting an increase of 1.3 percent on month and 13.7 percent on year. That follows the 5.2 percent monthly increase and the 18.6 percent yearly gain in August.

data.title: Wheat, corn, soybean futures sag as dollar firms
data.description:
Chicago wheat futures fell roughly 4% on Wednesday, giving up gains from the previous session as the dollar hit a 19-month high, making US grains less competitive globally, analysts said.

Corn fell 2.5% while soybeans posted more modest declines as lower crude oil added to bearish sentiment.

Chicago Board of Trade March wheat futures settled down 24-1/4 cents, or 3.97%, at $5.86 per bushel after hitting $5.85, the contract's lowest level since January.

CBOT December corn ended down 11-1/4 cents, or 2.52%, at $4.35-1/2 a bushel and January soybeans finished down 8-3/4 cents, or 0.71%, at $12.16-3/4 a bushel.

Strength in the dollar pressured the grains complex as well as other commodities including gold, coffee and cotton. The greenback firmed on expectations for an interest rate hike next month.

"The strength in the dollar is definitely into the grain markets," said Tom Fritz, a partner with EFG Group in Chicago.

"There is lots of technical selling involved here. The funds are adding to their wheat shorts. They're adding to their shorts in corn, and I believe they're still liquidating in soybeans," Fritz said.

Managed funds still held a net long position in CBOT soybean futures as of November 10, weekly data from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission showed.

Traders awaited a meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia for diplomatic developments on Russia's war in Ukraine. US President Donald Trump is expected to hold bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China on Thursday, in addition to the trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, US and Russian officials said.

Wheat had rallied on Tuesday after a Ukrainian attack destroyed the central road section of the Crimea bridge. Debris blocked navigation through the Sea of Azov, threatening further disruption to massive Russian wheat exports.

But with shipping traffic in the Azov-Black Sea zone already heavily reduced for months due to drone attacks and incoming Southern Hemisphere harvests set to bolster global supplies, market reaction was moderate, traders said.

Grain markets are also monitoring developments regarding US-China relations, with Chinese purchases of US agricultural goods a central part of the countries' ongoing trade truce.

data.title: UniCredit and Germany reach broad agreement on Commerzbank takeover
data.description:
Key points:
  • Major development in two-year takeover battle
  • Merged bank's German headquarters to remain in Frankfurt as listed entity
  • Germany drops demand to name two Commerzbank supervisory board members
  • UniCredit pledges to add German nationals to its board of directors

By Holger Hansen

UniCredit and Germany have reached agreement on the big sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, a major development in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

The agreement, laid out in a letter from UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil as well as a separate statement to Reuters from the German minister, states that the merged bank's German headquarters will remain in Frankfurt as a listed entity, a key German demand.

But Germany has given up its insistence on naming two supervisory board members to Commerzbank , in a concession to UniCredit.

A combination of UniCredit and Commerzbank would create a bank with more than €1.3 trillion ($1.4 trillion) in assets across two of the euro zone's ​largest economies in one of the most significant cross-border European banking deals in years.

In the letter dated November 18 and seen by Reuters, Orcel said he was "prepared to commit" to a series of binding principles and thanked Klingbeil for discussions "which have allowed us to find common ground."

UniCredit also pledged to put German nationals on UniCredit's board of directors.

Klingbeil, in his statement to Reuters, said Germany "supports a swift process and an orderly transition of control."

"We have reached common ground and UniCredit has made clear commitments to Germany as a business location, to the rights of Commerzbank employees and to a continued constructive dialogue with the works council in the further process," Klingbeil said, referring to a body of elected employee representatives.

Orcel pounced on Commerzbank in 2024, catching the lender and the government off guard by discreetly building up a holding. Commerzbank and Berlin tried to prevent the takeover, ​but gave in after UniCredit amassed a stake nearing ​50%.

The German government holds a 13.3% stake in Commerzbank following a bailout during the global financial crisis.

The sale of the federal government's stake remains an open question. Orcel's letter said UniCredit's agreements "set the basis for the disposal of the government's stake", but Klingbeil's statement contains no commitment to sell.

Klingbeil ​and Orcel met in September on the Italian bank's hostile €45 billion approach. Both called the talks "constructive" but differences remained.

Since then, the European Central Bank, the European Commission and the US Federal Reserve have given a green light to a deal, clearing regulatory hurdles.

Earlier this month, Commerzbank said that it was "convinced" a deal between the two ‌banks could create value, in a markedly more bullish stance on a potential tie-up it had long resisted.

($1 = 0.9115 euros)

data.title: Kazakhstan expects FAA blessing for direct US flights ahead of Trump-hosted G20 meeting
data.description:
By Allison Lampert and David Shepardson

Kazakhstan hopes to get a coveted US safety rating in time for a December G20 summit that the Central Asian country's president is expected to attend in Miami at the invitation of host President Donald Trump.

Talgat Lastayev, vice minister of transport for Kazakhstan, said on Tuesday he is expecting news in December on whether his country will get a category 1 safety rating that would allow direct flights to the United States.

Starting direct US flights would be a boost for landlocked Kazakhstan, which is banking on investment in its fast-growing aviation system to drive air traffic and develop its resource-rich economy.

The preliminary result of a Federal Aviation Administration review was quite good, following an audit in Kazakhstan in September, Lastayev said in an interview.

“We expect that in December before this great meeting we will get officially category one,” Lastayev said about the G20 summit, adding that the decision must be taken by the FAA.

The FAA currently does not have a rating for Kazakhstan. An agency spokesperson said the FAA does not comment on the details of reviews.

Trump has sought to deepen US ties with Central Asia, where Russia and China have traditionally held major sway.

Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev was invited to the G20 being held on December 14-15.

Lastayev spoke on the sidelines of the International Civil Aviation Organization's global transport conference in Montreal, where Kazakhstan is vying to join the UN agency's governing council.

The country has gone from 10 million passengers a year before the pandemic to 31 million passengers a year, and expects to double traffic to about 60 million in the next five years, he said. Lastayev said airlines are expected to launch direct flights between Kazakhstan and the United States by the end of 2027.

Kazakhstan has benefited from traffic due to airspace disruptions to its north, since US and European carriers are avoiding Russian airspace and due to conflict south of the country in the Middle East.

“Kazakhstan lays exactly in the middle, like a belt in the middle between two restricted regions,” he said.

data.title: UGI to Spin Off Liquefied Petroleum Gas Business
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

UGI plans to spin off its global liquefied petroleum gas business into two public companies.

The distributor of energy products on Wednesday said the spinoff, approved by its board, is part of the company's transformation strategy and should position both companies for long-term growth. The separation is expected to be completed during the second half of 2027.

After the spinoff's completion, the new UGI will be a natural gas infrastructure company for customers in the mid-atlantic regions. The new liquefied petroleum gas company is expected to be a distributor in Europe, while also being a retail propane distributor in the U.S.

Under the proposed spinoff plan, UGI shareholders will retain their current shares and receive a pro-rata distribution of shares of the new LPG company's stock. After the spinoff, the new UGI may retain a stake of up to 20% in the new LPG company.

The spinoff came as UGI on Wednesday posted a fourth-quarter profit of $8 million, or 4 cents a share, compared with a loss of $13 million, or 6 cents a share, the year earlier.

Revenue fell to $1.16 billion from $1.2 billion the year before.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: Nvidia's deeper risks predate Huang's scandal: McGeever
data.description:
By Jamie McGeever

As investors digest the latest twists in scandal-hit Nvidia's evolving drama, it's worth remembering that they had already started to sour on the world's erstwhile AI darling well before former CEO Jensen Huang resigned. That may be far more worrying for the AI trade.

Nvidia offered investors some relief on Tuesday, delivering bumper third-quarter revenue and earnings, as well as sales projections that exceeded Wall Street estimates. Nvidia's shares rose as much as 5% in extended trading.

This comes after Nvidia's share price tanked nearly 40% from its record high on October 6, wiping some $2 trillion off its market capitalization and knocking the firm off its pedestal as the world's most valuable company.

Importantly, the bulk of Nvidia’s share price decline came before Huang admitted on November 8 to having an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed and alleged Chinese spy. His resignation came four days later following allegations of improper relationships with Nvidia employees.

There is suddenly a plethora of reasons why investors may think twice about buying Nvidia shares, such as trust and accountability, the board's leadership, and US national security concerns amid external investigations, including a reported probe by the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

But just as worrying may be the gnawing unease investors have about Nvidia's customer financing, long-term demand for its chips, and the AI business model – all of which predate the scandal.

'DISCIPLINED' APPROACH

Nvidia's fall from favor has been rapid. This should probably come as no surprise, given how meteoric its ascent was.

It is one of only 10 firms since 1960 to hold the title of the largest company in the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX, according to JPMorgan Private Bank's Michael Cembalest. That’s a remarkably small number and would be even smaller were it not for Cisco's three days at the top in 2000.

Nvidia's epic rise was the fastest of them all. Its share of the S&P 500 in December 2022 was 1%. By May this year, it was 8.5%. Revenue and profit growth have exploded thanks to soaring demand for its chips from hyperscalers and so-called “neocloud” AI partners that Nvidia has often helped finance.

It's unclear how committed interim CEO and former chief financial officer Colette Kress is to this model. On the earnings call on Tuesday, she said Nvidia will be “disciplined" and selective in its capital commitments, investments, and guarantees, although she said there are no plans to change its backstops for "neocloud" companies.

Should that position change, however, companies like CoreWeave , Nebius , IREN and Applied Digital , whose shares have already tumbled steeply in recent months, could fall further.

BIS WARNING

This shines a spotlight on the AI vendor financing trend. The Bank for International Settlements published a special report on the subject last month, which found that between 2021 and 2025, nearly 30% of all AI firms’ investment deals by value involved an AI firm on the other side. Meanwhile, 55% of incoming investments in AI firms came from other AI firms.

The authors warned that such circular relationships can artificially inflate demand, which can become a problem if revenue growth and real end-user demand slow. The AI flywheel could then go into reverse, potentially leading to "significant financial market volatility," the BIS warned.

This risk is exacerbated by the fact that many of these deals are opaque, complex, and private, making them difficult to monitor and supervise.

"These risks may be magnified by the growing use of private credit and special purpose vehicles to finance AI infrastructure, which can create hidden leverage and interconnected exposures that amplify financial stress during downturns," the BIS authors wrote.

The AI sector is clearly in a downturn on Wall Street right now, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping nearly 30% in the last six weeks. AI’s crown jewel may have just released sparkling results, but they are not bright enough to obscure the deep-rooted, mounting concerns about the AI ecosystem.

(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

data.title: US FDA approves Regeneron's drug for generalized myasthenia gravis
data.description:
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' drug to treat adults with a type of rare autoimmune disease called generalized myasthenia gravis, the company said on Wednesday.

The drug, cemdisiran, branded as Livsayis, was approved for adults with generalized myasthenia gravis who test positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies, the most common form of the disease.

Generalized myasthenia gravis causes muscle weakness affecting movement, speech, swallowing and breathing.

Livsayis, which is to be injected under the skin once every three months, is the only US-approved treatment for the disease, Regeneron said.

data.title: PANW Stock Soars 11% After-Hours On Q1 Earnings Beat, $4.5B Acquisition Announcement
data.description:
Key points:
  • Total revenue for the quarter reached $3.44 billion, outpacing consensus forecasts, while earnings per share hit $1.05. 
  • Applied Compute acquisition to bolster PANW’s enterprise capabilities in open-weight AI models. 
  • Palo Alto expects full-year revenue at $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock gained about 11% after-hours on Wednesday after topping analyst expectations for its first quarter ending October, along with a raised outlook on the backdrop of concerns regarding artificial intelligence-powered cyber threats.

For the fiscal first quarter, the company reported earnings of $1.05 per share, beating analysts' $0.97 estimate.

Total revenue surged 39% to $3.44 billion, up from $2.47 billion during the same period last year and beating expectations of $3.31 billion.

Annual recurring revenue (ARR), the yearly income a subscription or contract business expects from active customers, climbed 66% year-over-year to hit $9.73 billion. ARR is one of the key metrics analysts use when evaluating companies like Palo Alto.

“As AI reshapes the threat landscape, we must continually evolve to protect our customers and enable them to adopt AI securely,” CEO Nikesh Arora said in a release.

A wave of recent high-profile system outages that hit financial institutions, airlines, and enterprise infrastructure have prompted businesses to significantly boost their digital security investments, directly aiding cybersecurity firms like Palo Alto Networks and its peers like Zscaler (ZS) and CrowdStrike (CRWD).

The $4.5 Billion Applied Compute Deal

Palo Alto Networks announced an agreement to acquire Applied Compute, an AI model platform, in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion.

Applied Compute provides an infrastructure environment enabling enterprises to train, refine, and deploy open-weight artificial intelligence models and autonomous agents. By opting for open-weight systems over proprietary closed frameworks, organizations can download and run model parameters directly within their private infrastructure, creating a tailored, budget-friendly approach with enhanced data governance.

“If it works, I think this will dwarf the ability that we have in cybersecurity,” Arora said on an earnings call. “This could be bigger than what we do.“

Q2 and Full-Year 2027 Outlook

For the upcoming second quarter ending January 2027, the cybersecurity stock expects its total revenue to be in the range of $3.530 billion to $3.550 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 36% to 37% and above analyst expectations.

For the full year, it expects revenue in the range of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, above expectations of $14.16 billion.

data.title: Earnings Backdrop for Australian General Insurers Improves — Market Talk
data.description: The earnings backdrop for Australian general insurers has improved rather than deteriorated since June, says Jefferies. Central banks are raising rates again. The strongest El Niño weather event on record is building in the Pacific. Reinsurance capacity remains abundant. "Against this, commercial cycles continue to soften, New Zealand remains problematic, and AI disintermediation has emerged as a new source of share price volatility," says analyst Simon Fitzgerald. Jefferies has a "buy" call on IAG, its top pick in the sector. IAG is struggling to convince regulators to approve its alliance with the Royal Automobile Club of Western Australia. Jefferies acknowledges that deal may ultimately prove challenging. Still, a material on-market share buyback by IAG would be a second-best option, it says. Jefferies has "hold" calls on Suncorp and QBE Insurance. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)

data.title: Plurilock Security Inc. Announces Shareholder Approval for Plan of Arrangement with Quantum eMotion Corp.
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Plurilock Security Inc. (OTCQB: PLCKF) ("Plurilock" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that, at the special meeting (the "Meeting") of holders (the "Shareholders") of common shares of Plurilock (each, a "Plurilock Share" and, collectively, the "Plurilock Shares") held on November 18, 2026, Shareholders voted in favour of the special resolution (the "Arrangement Resolution") approving the previously announced plan of arrangement (the "Arrangement") with Quantum eMotion Corp. ("QeM"). The Arrangement is being completed pursuant to the terms and conditions of a definitive arrangement agreement between Plurilock and QeM dated September 28, 2026 (the "Arrangement Agreement").

Under the Arrangement, QeM will acquire all of the issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares. Shareholders will receive C$0.084 in cash and 0.0763 of a common share of QeM (each whole common share of QeM, a "QeM Share") in exchange for each Plurilock Share they hold (together, the "Consideration"), implying total consideration of C$0.28 per Plurilock Share. Further, all outstanding options to acquire Plurilock Shares ("Plurilock Options") will be cancelled in exchange for QeM Shares and cash in the same proportions as the Consideration having a value equal to the amount (if any) by which C$0.28 exceeds the applicable exercise price per Plurilock Option. All outstanding restricted share units will vest immediately prior to the effective time of the Arrangement and be settled for the Consideration. All outstanding warrants and convertible debentures of Plurilock will, in accordance with their terms and without further action by the holders thereof, entitle the holders to receive, upon exercise or conversion, the Consideration in lieu of Plurilock Shares.

Shareholders holding a total of 68,226,137 Plurilock Shares were represented in person or by proxy at the Meeting, representing 60.38% of the 112,989,001 issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares entitled to vote as of October 1, 2026, the record date for the Meeting.

The Arrangement required the approval of: (i) at least two-thirds (66⅔%) of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting; and (ii) a majority of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting, excluding Plurilock Shares held by "interested parties" as defined in Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101").

At the Meeting, 99.58% of the votes cast by Shareholders (99.54% after excluding Plurilock Shares required to be excluded under MI 61-101) were in favour of the Arrangement Resolution.

The Company will seek a final order (the "Final Order") of the Supreme Court of British Columbia (the "Court") to approve the Arrangement on November 20, 2026. Completion of the Arrangement is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions for a transaction of this nature, including receipt of the Final Order. Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the closing conditions, it is expected that the Arrangement will be completed shortly after the receipt of the Final Order. Following completion of the Arrangement, it is expected that the Plurilock Shares will be delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV").

About Quantum eMotion Corp.

Quantum eMotion Corp. (NYSE American: QNC) (FSE: 34Q0) is developing quantum-secure cybersecurity technologies designed to protect digital systems, communications and data in an increasingly complex cyber-threat environment. QeM's technology portfolio combines quantum-generated entropy, quantum-safe cryptography and cybersecurity technologies designed for applications across enterprise, cloud, communications, critical infrastructure and other security-sensitive environments. For more information, visit www.quantumemotion.com.

About Plurilock Security Inc.

Plurilock sells cybersecurity solutions and delivers critical IT and cybersecurity services to public- and private-sector organizations. Through its operating businesses and predecessor operations, Plurilock has a 25-plus-year operating history, serves hundreds of customers and maintains procurement and contract channels in Canada, the United States and NATO. Its capabilities include Critical Services, cybersecurity and IT modernization, managed services, data protection, cloud security, identity and access management, and AI-enabled security technologies. For more information, visit www.plurilock.com.

data.title: Elon Musk Likens Sacking of Jensen Huang to Benching Michael Jordan — WSJ
data.description:
By Jack Morphet

Tech billionaire Elon Musk doesn't think former Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang has been disloyal to the U.S. and found his ouster shocking.

"It's like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you're on a winning streak," Musk said at Wednesday's New York Times DealBook Summit. "It doesn't seem like a good thing for shareholders."

Musk appeared remotely from China, where he is traveling with President Trump. He said he would hire Huang, adding, "But who wouldn't?"

He rebuffed repeated questions about Huang when he was asked whether he had spoken to Trump about the former chip executive's future. "We're not on the board," he said.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
